rinCaseStudy.metaDescription: A case study of the RIN Aesthetic Practice website in Charlottesville: brand-aligned design, treatment pages, online booking, and fast, accessible performance.
rinCaseStudy.title: RIN Aesthetic Practice
rinCaseStudy.subhead: A calm, fast website for a medical aesthetics studio in Charlottesville, built to turn first-time visitors into booked consultations.

meta.label: Services
meta.value: Brand-aligned UI, web development, booking integration

overview: RIN Aesthetic Practice offers medical aesthetics treatments in Charlottesville, Virginia. The practice needed a website that matched its refined, intentional, natural positioning, made its treatments easy to understand, and let prospective clients book a consultation without a phone call.
We designed and built the site from the ground up: brand-aligned interface, treatment and concern pages, a results gallery, a small shop, and online booking, all tuned for speed and accessibility.

built.label: Treatment and concern pages
built.text: Content organized by what a visitor is trying to solve, not only by procedure name.

built.label: Online booking
built.text: Consultation requests flow straight to the practice, with no third-party widget.

built.label: Results gallery
built.text: A lightweight gallery that loads fast on mobile, where most visitors browse.

built.label: Shop
built.text: A simple product section for the skincare the practice carries.

built.label: Brand-aligned UI
built.text: Gold on dark walnut, matching the physical space, with large photography and generous spacing.

rinCaseStudy.design: The practice's interior sets the tone: dark walnut slats, warm lighting, and a gold logotype. We carried that into the site with a near-black palette, gold accents reserved for actions, and serif display type for headings. Everything else stays quiet so the photography and the booking buttons do the work.

bellhouseCaseStudy.metaDescription: A case study of the Bellhouse Real Estate Group website in Charlottesville: team-managed listings, sold history, area guides, an interactive service map, and a home-value lead flow.
bellhouseCaseStudy.title: Bellhouse Real Estate Group
bellhouseCaseStudy.subhead: A content-driven website for a three-agent Charlottesville real estate team: live listings, sold history, area guides, and a home-value lead flow, all managed by the team themselves.

meta.label: Client
meta.value: Bellhouse Real Estate Group, eXp Realty

meta.label: Services
meta.value: Web development, content system, MLS integration

overview: Bellhouse Real Estate Group is a three-agent team with eXp Realty serving Charlottesville and Central Virginia. Most agent sites are a brokerage template with a search box. Bellhouse wanted something closer to a local publication: their own listings and sales, guides to the counties they work in, notes from the agents, and a clear way for homeowners to request a valuation.

We built a custom site with a team login, so listings, sold records, area pages, and notes are updated by the agents without a developer. Search hands off to the brokerage's full MLS tool, while everything that makes the team distinctive lives on their own domain.

built.label: Listings and sold history
built.text: The team's own active listings with tour requests, and a sold table that totals the year automatically.

built.label: Area guides
built.text: Pages for Charlottesville and eleven surrounding counties, each with local photography and the neighborhoods the team knows.

built.label: Interactive service map
built.text: A hand-built SVG map of Charlottesville and the eleven counties the team covers, with hover states that link to each area guide. No map service, no tracking, loads instantly.

built.label: Team login
built.text: A private admin where agents add listings, mark sales, and publish notes, with no CMS to learn.

built.label: Home-value lead flow
built.text: A valuation request answered by an agent, positioned against automated estimates.

built.label: MLS handoff
built.text: The search form passes location and filters straight into the brokerage MLS search.

built.label: Compliance
built.text: Fair Housing statement, MLS attribution, accessibility page, and the agent license details required in Virginia.

bellhouseCaseStudy.design: Real estate sites tend to shout. This one uses a navy and white palette, a serif display face for headings, and large regional photography so the Blue Ridge and the city do the selling. Agent photos appear throughout, since people hire an agent, not a brand. Dense pages such as the sold table and the areas grid are built as real tables and lists so they stay readable on a phone and legible to screen readers.
